newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends up on bean rally, stocks cited.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends up on bean rally, stocks cited.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher as the neighboring soybean pit staged an impressive rally with that market surging nearly half the daily trading limit on relentless fund buying into the close, traders said.
"It definitely was following beans," said Paul Haugens, vice president for Chicag-based trade house FIMAT Futures. "There might have been a little support because they didn't increase the carryout."
Some thought USDA Wednesday may show a slight hike in its outlook for 1996-97 U.S. corn carryout but the government left intact its figures set in the January Supply/Demand Report.
USDA early Wednesday, in its February Supply/Demand Report, pegged 1996-97 U.S. corn carryout at 959 million bushels, unchanged from the January report.

Chartists early Wednesday said first support in the March was $2.71-1/2 and second support was at $2.69-1/2. The session low for March was $2.71-1/4. First resistance for March was $2.73 and second resistance was $2.75. The session high for March was $2.74.
Corn closed 1/4 to 1-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with March up 1-1/4 at $2.73-3/4 a bushel.
Refco Inc bought one million bushels each of March and May, Tenco Inc bought 1.5 million bushels of March and The Chicago Corp bought one million bushels of March, traders said.
Cargill Inc sold three million bushels each of March and July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 45,000 contracts, above the 31,540 traded Tuesday.
In corn options, LIT America bought 500 March $2.70 puts at 1-5/8 cents, Tradelink Futures bought 500 July $2.80 calls at s at six cents.
Corn options volume was estimated at 13,000 contracts, above the 12,693 traded Tuesday.
